$comment: Advisories knowingly accepted in the dependency ranges the generators emit. Every entry needs a reason and a reviewed date — an entry with no route to a fix is legitimate, an entry nobody has looked at in a year is not. Keyed by GHSA id.

advisories.reason: Vulnerable range is >=6.0.0 <7.18.0, so no 6.x release clears it. react-app pins react-router-dom 6.30.4; the only remediation is React Router 7, which merges react-router-dom into react-router and changes several APIs — a breaking migration for every generated app, not a version bump. Revisit when react-app moves to v7.

Same 6.x/7.x split as GHSA-wrjc-x8rr-h8h6 above (vulnerable >=6.4.0 <7.18.0), and reached only through deserializeErrors() in SSR hydration, which the generated apps do not use — they are client-rendered behind nginx.

Reached through drizzle-kit's deprecated @esbuild-kit/core-utils dependency, which pins an old esbuild. No 0.31.x release of drizzle-kit drops it; drizzle-kit 1.0 does, but is still beta. drizzle-kit is a dev-only migration CLI, and the advisory is a dev-server CORS issue that needs the developer to visit a hostile page while it runs. Revisit when drizzle-kit 1.0 is stable.
